text: Working with APIs is an essential skill for modern developers. An API allows two applications to communicate by sending HTTP requests, such as GET or POST, to a server. The server usually responds with data in JSON format, which is easy to read and parse. Before you can access most APIs, you need authentication, often through an API key or token, to prove your identity. It is also important to respect rate limits, which restrict how many requests you can make within a certain time. Finally, always include error handling in your code, because network problems and invalid responses can happen at any time.
